narrative.arc: Jamaica → journey → Toronto → music → identity → future.

beats.title: THE STREET ALREADY HAD A BASSLINE.
beats.body: Heat on zinc. Hills holding the back of the mix. Sound-system pressure — not a postcard. Origin as climate: the ear learned outdoors first.

beats.title: WHAT YOU KEEP ON THE ROAD.
beats.body: Vegetation thins. The road regularizes. Warm haze cools. Jamaica recedes behind the camera; another grid assembles in front of it.

beats.title: BRICK. NIGHT BUS. WINTER AIR.
beats.body: A colder city that taught the record to sit. Bay windows. Concrete. A needle on the skyline. A street you drop into, then lift out of.

beats.title: THE PRACTICE IS THE PRESENT.
beats.body: MPC 2000XL. Rhodes. SP-404. Four-hour sessions: drums first, silk second, hook last. The room holds both climates in one pocket.

tapes.title: SILK ON THE 808
tapes.caption: Silk on the 808 — 86 BPM, F minor. After-hours body music. The 808 is the chest, not the drop.

tapes.title: PRESSURE SKETCH 3
tapes.blurb: Raw bounce. Chopped horns. Kick in the gutter.
tapes.caption: Pressure Sketch 3 — 93 BPM, B minor. Booth bounce, chopped horns, kick in the gutter. A sketch you can still sit in.

tapes.title: AFTERIMAGE CHORDS
tapes.caption: Afterimage Chords — 72 BPM, D-flat. Slow architecture. Gospel voicings that refuse to resolve on the one.

tapes.title: GRID DIG
tapes.blurb: Filtered break, chopped soul, mandatory nod.
tapes.caption: Grid Dig — 97 BPM, G minor. Filtered break, chopped soul, mandatory nod. Crate logic, not crate costume.
